slides.text: THE PRISON THAT INVENTED SOLITARY CONFINEMENT
Philadelphia, 1829. Eastern State Penitentiary opens with a new idea: total isolation.
Each prisoner lived alone. When they left their cell, guards put a hood over their head so they couldn't see anyone.
The only light came from a small window in the ceiling. Some called it the Eye of God.
Charles Dickens visited in 1842. He wrote that the system was cruel and wrong.
Its most famous inmate: Al Capone, in 1929. His cell had rugs, furniture... and a radio.
In 1945, a dozen inmates escaped through a tunnel they had dug. All were caught. Some within minutes.
The prison closed in 1971 and was left to rot for decades.
Today it's a museum. Staff and visitors report footsteps, faces and whispers in the cellblocks. Could you last a night?
